correctness.rationale: For positive fixed parameters, columns of the weighted tree shift have disjoint supports, giving an exact Aluthge recursion. A normalized softmax identity and contractive forced scalar log recurrence establish operator norm convergence. The exact orthogonal-error identity and uniform geometric remainder bounds separate four nonzero sharp asymptotic coefficients; all-equal-tail and \(H=0\) are handled explicitly. A standalone 6,800-assertion checker replays finite-depth independent transformations and formulas but is not substituted for the proof. No unproved bound is used as a theorem.

value.rationale: General infinite-dimensional Aluthge convergence can fail, so isolating norm-convergent noncompact tree shifts is a motivated problem. An exact phase transition at \(1-t\) equal to the largest subdominant radial ratio, with quadrature resonance and cancellation of a slower root relaxation mode, is a structural classification across all finite branch counts and all positive tail/root weights. The exact operator norm, rather than entrywise convergence or a finite sample, makes the result useful for asymptotic stability of the transform.
